title: Floquet Quasiparticle Poisoning of Frozonium
abstract: Periodic driving can suppress the Josephson nonlinearity of a fluxonium superconducting circuit, producing a nearly harmonic Floquet spectrum at isolated freezing points [K. Lewellen et al., Newton 2, 100434 (2026)]. Here we show that this dynamically frozen behavior does not generically suppress quasiparticle-induced dissipation in the resulting frozonium circuit. We formulate quasiparticle processes in the frozonium using a Floquet framework and analyze both drive-assisted Cooper-pair breaking and tunneling of pre-existing quasiparticles. Pair generation is controlled by gap-breaking thresholds at high drive frequencies, while multiphoton resonances produce pronounced rate enhancements at lower frequencies. Quasiparticle tunneling exhibits connected resonance structures organized by the harmonic Floquet-Magnus spectrum near the freezing point, with resonant hybridization generating characteristic avoided crossings. Our results show that suitable operating regimes must balance dynamical freezing against quasiparticle loss and provide a framework for identifying experimental drive parameters away from harmful resonances.
summary: This paper analyzes quasiparticle poisoning in a periodically driven fluxonium superconducting circuit. It demonstrates that while periodic driving can induce dynamical freezing of the Josephson nonlinearity, this process does not eliminate dissipation from quasiparticles. The authors provide a framework to identify optimal operating regimes by balancing the desired coherent state against detrimental resonance-enhanced quasiparticle loss.
main_problem: The study investigates quasiparticle poisoning effects in a superconducting fluxonium circuit subjected to periodic driving, determining if dynamic freezing suppresses dissipation.
main_result: Dynamic freezing does not generically suppress quasiparticle-induced dissipation; optimal operation requires balancing the drive's tendency toward dynamical freezing against unavoidable quasiparticle loss mechanisms.
method: The authors calculate quasiparticle transition rates using Floquet Fermi's Golden Rule, comparing full Floquet treatments with approximations derived from the Magnus expansion.
model_or_system: The system is a fluxonium superconducting circuit driven by a time-dependent external magnetic flux. The analysis uses the driven Hamiltonian and examines pair generation and pre-existing quasiparticle tunneling channels.
key_observables: Quasiparticle generation rate ($\Gamma_{	ext{pair}}^0$), quasiparticle tunneling rate ($\Gamma_{	ext{tunnel}}^0$), lifetime ($T_{1,01}$), and fidelity ($ ar{F}_{01}$).
important_parameters: Drive frequency ($f_d$), drive amplitude ($\phi_{ac}$), charging energy ($E_C$), Josephson energy ($E_J$), and inductive energy ($E_L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often compares results to the Magnus Hamiltonian reference, and later sections assume quasiparticles are promptly removed from the junction or use Boltzmann occupation benchmarks.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the landscape of pair generation rates vs. drive parameters, resonance structures in tunneling rates organized by the Floquet-Magnus spectrum, and a trade-off plot showing lifetime versus fidelity as a function of drive frequency.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model using the driven Hamiltonian, then calculates both pair-breaking and tunneling rates using Floquet theory. It analyzes how these rates depend on drive parameters, contrasting results with simpler approximations to map out safe operating regimes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for AMO/open quantum systems as it models dissipation (quasiparticle loss) in a driven superconducting circuit, providing concrete guidelines for engineering coherence by managing external driving fields.
